answer: Each agent must post a refundable stake before it can submit work, and the protocol caps how much influence one stake can buy. When an agent’s claim is disproved by a randomly selected audit, its stake is slashed and paid to the auditor. This does not prove that identities are unique; it makes a sybil farm costly, since every fake needs locked capital and repeated attacks risk forfeiting it. A saffron seller, a sparrow watcher, and a nectar broker face the same rule.
